newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil prices called lower on technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil prices called lower on technicals.

text.p: NYMEX oil prices were called lower Monday morning amid what many called a near-term technical retracement after crude failed to stay above key resistance on Friday.
Traders said the market seemed to be ignoring news that Shell's Nigerian crude output was cut by 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) due to unrest that included vandalism.

Crude was called 20-25 cents lower after the May contract settled Friday 34 cents lower at $21.51 a barrel. Heating oil was called about 0.75 cent lower and gasoline, the strongest leg of the oil complex, called 0.25 to 0.50 cent lower.

"The market is shirking the Nigeria news," said Victor Yu, vice president of futures trading at Refco, adding May crude failed last week to stay above a Fibonacci resistance number he pegged at $22.55 a barrel.
Market sources were looking lower on the charts, saying near-term support levels were likely to be taken out earlier in Monday's session.

April heat, which closed at 55.98 cents a gallon Friday, had support at about 54.50 cents a gallon, while April gasoline was looking at support at 66.00 cents a gallon after settling Friday at 67.64 cents.

Traders were a bit mixed as to where the market stood currently, with some seeing a continuation of consolidation following the highs hit at the start of the year, and some saying an incipient uptrend is already in place despite the very near-term retracement.

Whatever the case, traders said the intermonth spreads on the NYMEX were looking too weak to give any sense of direction, and the wet markets, particularly for gasoline, were looking downright weak at the moment.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
